- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias, especially if recent prices are rising.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction to prevent overreaction.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early forecast periods — if true outcome deviates sharply from forecast, adjust future predictions toward historical mean of last 5–7 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses early correction or reversal signals; prioritize sentiment + recent 3–5 day price behavior over long-term trends.
- When sentiment history contains multiple 0.2 spikes, model tends to overreact; apply dampening factor to forecast increments after 2–3 consecutive positive sentiment days.
